questions.questionText: SECTION A - COMPOSITION (Choose ONE: Question 1a OR Question 1b). 1(a) Describe a clean-up campaign that takes place in your area. In your composition, cover: who started the clean-up campaign in your area; why it was introduced; what people do on the day it takes place; who supplies the materials/equipment used (e.g. bins, rakes, gloves, masks); and why this day matters to your school or community. Write about 80-120 words, and give your composition a suitable heading.
questions.explanation: This is a REAL question from the ZIMSEC Grade 7 English Paper 2, October 2022 session, reconstructed from the official Examiners' Report's marking pegs (not a fabricated practice question). Marking guidance from the real report: candidates must describe what USUALLY/REGULARLY happens (an ongoing, recurring activity), not narrate a single past event - this was the single most common error nationally, where many candidates wrote about 'a day when we did a clean-up' instead of 'what we always do when we clean up'. A suitable heading earns 1 mark. Nationally in 2022, the strongest scripts scored 14-16 out of 20, while most candidates fell in the 10-11 (satisfactory) or 5-9 (weak) range - common weaknesses were spelling errors on the words 'environment' and 'campaign' (both given in the question itself), and shallow treatment of WHY the campaign was introduced and its IMPORTANCE to the community, which most candidates barely addressed. For 'who introduced the clean-up', real candidate answers nationally ranged widely and were all accepted - Village Head, President, First Lady, School Head, and Ministry of Health were all seen; this peg was answered by virtually all candidates. Nice integration point: many candidates correctly listed real cleaning tools/materials (plastic bins, rakes, gloves, masks), which examiners noted as evidence of cross-subject integration with Agriculture.

questions.questionText: SECTION A - COMPOSITION (Choose ONE: Question 1a OR Question 1b). 1(b) Write a report to be read by other learners, explaining how you benefited from winning a scholarship. In your report, cover: how you got the scholarship; how you felt when you found out about it; how the scholarship has helped you and your parents; and what advice you would give to other learners. Use the correct report format (From / To / Subject / Date) and write about 80-120 words.
questions.explanation: This is a REAL question from the ZIMSEC Grade 7 English Paper 2, October 2022 session, reconstructed from the official Examiners' Report's marking pegs. Marking guidance from the real report: this must be written as a REPORT (From/To/Subject/Date format, or at least a suitable heading), NOT as a letter - a common national error was candidates ending with 'Yours faithfully' or 'Yours sincerely', which is letter format and is incorrect here. Nationally, most candidates explained how they got the scholarship (usually through academic excellence, or through sport, singing, dancing or quiz competitions) and how they felt (commonly: happy, excited, or 'perplexed' - a very frequently used word by 2022 candidates). However, most candidates skipped or gave very weak answers on HOW THE SCHOLARSHIP HELPED THEIR PARENTS (the expected answer involves saving money/reducing financial burden on the family) - this peg was the weakest-answered part nationally.

questions.questionText: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(a): According to the passage, what was the waterfall called?
questions.explanation: REAL verified ZIMSEC answer from the passage 'Day out at the Waterfall'. Write the FULL proper name, correctly capitalised ('Nyakuna Falls'), not just 'Nyakuna' alone. Nationally in 2022, about 70% of candidates answered this correctly, but many lost the mark either by giving only the partial name 'Nyakuna', or by writing 'falls' with a lower-case f, which the passage treats as part of a proper noun.

questions.questionText: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(b): Why did the driver drive slowly along the road to the waterfall?
questions.correctAnswer: Because the road was bumpy (rough/uneven, so the car had to move slowly).
questions.explanation: REAL verified ZIMSEC answer. Write this as a full, correctly ordered sentence in your own words - do not simply lift the exact sentence from the passage word-for-word, as this loses marks for lack of focus even when it contains the right idea. Nationally, just over half of candidates answered correctly; wrong word order in candidates' own sentences was a common cause of lost marks.

questions.questionText: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(c): What kind of sound did the water from the waterfall make?
questions.explanation: REAL verified ZIMSEC answer. Either 'The water produced a roaring sound' or the restated form 'A roaring sound was produced by the falling water' were both accepted. Most marks lost nationally were due to grammatical errors made while trying to restate the sentence in full, rather than not knowing the answer itself.

questions.questionText: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(d): How did everyone feel when they first saw the waterfall?
questions.correctAnswer: Dumbfounded/speechless (or any accepted synonym such as amazed, stunned, flabbergasted, or perplexed).
questions.explanation: REAL verified ZIMSEC answer. Only about 25% of candidates nationally scored full marks here - the main reason was limited vocabulary, as many candidates could not think of a synonym for 'dumbfounded', and others who did know the word misspelt it (e.g. 'dumpfounded').

questions.questionText: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(e): Find a single word in the passage which has the same meaning as 'at the same time'.
questions.explanation: REAL verified ZIMSEC answer. This was one of the hardest questions on the real 2022 paper - only about 20% of candidates scored full marks nationally, mainly because of vocabulary gaps and because some candidates who identified the right word still misspelt 'simultaneously'.

questions.questionText: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(f): When Tafadzwa's sister said 'Break the ice, Tafadzwa!', what was she telling Tafadzwa to do?
questions.correctAnswer: She was telling Tafadzwa to be the FIRST person to get into the pool/water (not simply instructing her to get into the water in general).
questions.explanation: REAL verified ZIMSEC answer. This tests understanding of the IDIOM 'break the ice' (to be first to do something, easing the way for others), not its literal meaning. This was one of the most commonly missed questions nationally in 2022 - most candidates only wrote 'she told her to get into the water', missing the essential idea of being FIRST, and some candidates misunderstood the idiom literally, writing about breaking blocks of ice. Interesting examiner insight from the real report: the question paper's own examiners noted that this question felt MISPLACED in the sequence - since it tests a high-order idiomatic/figurative-language skill, it should have been positioned later among the comprehension questions (following Bloom's Taxonomy, from simple recall through to complex), not placed in the middle where easier recall questions surrounded it.

questions.questionText: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(g): What does the word 'famous', as used in the passage, mean?
questions.explanation: REAL verified ZIMSEC answer. This was a relatively accessible question - just over 40% of candidates nationally gave an acceptably correct definition, though some of the definitions offered were vague or unconvincing.

questions.questionText: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(h): Who is the narrator (the person telling the story) in this passage?
questions.explanation: REAL verified ZIMSEC answer. This was the EASIEST question on the real 2022 paper - roughly 80% of candidates nationally answered correctly, largely because Tafadzwa was the only proper name clearly repeated throughout the passage.

questions.questionText: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(i): Why did the mother ask the children to pick up litter before leaving?
questions.correctAnswer: So that they would leave the place clean / spotlessly clean / litter-free.
questions.explanation: REAL verified ZIMSEC answer. Over 60% of candidates nationally scored correctly, since the reason was stated fairly directly in the passage; a common spelling mistake nationally was writing 'live' instead of 'leave'.

questions.questionText: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(j): The writer says the day ended too quickly for her. Explain, in your own words, why she felt that way.
questions.correctAnswer: She felt that way because she was enjoying herself (enjoying the play/picnic/outing) and wanted the fun to continue - simply saying 'she wanted more fun' without linking it to already enjoying the day was not accepted as a complete answer.
questions.explanation: REAL verified ZIMSEC answer. This was a high-order 'evaluation' question, and was by far the HARDEST question on the real 2022 national paper - fewer than 5% of candidates scored the mark, since most answers ('she wanted to have more fun') failed to show that she was ALREADY enjoying herself and simply wished it could continue, which is what the expected answer required.

questions.questionText: SECTION B - COMPREHENSION ('Day out at the Waterfall'). Question 2(k) SUMMARY (5 marks): In not more than 60 words, write a summary of what the writer and her family members did at the falls. Begin your summary from the time the writer removed her shoes, to the time they prepared to leave the place. The real exam paper supplied a specific required opening phrase for this summary (not reproduced here, as the source report quotes candidates' guidance about it without quoting the exact phrase itself) - in your own practice, begin directly with the actions, naming Tafadzwa and her family clearly, and write in the THIRD person (not first person 'I').
questions.explanation: REAL verified ZIMSEC marking guidance. The real marking scheme for this question had 7 possible scoring points/actions; a maximum of 4 of these points could be credited for marks, plus a further +1 mark available for consistently good grammar. Marking rules from the real 2022 report: (1) only ACTIONS within the specified time window count (from removing shoes to preparing to leave) - do not summarise the whole passage, and candidates who summarised the whole text instead of just this window lost marks; (2) always name WHO did each action clearly (e.g. 'Tafadzwa splashed water at her sister', not a vague 'they'), since pronouns like 'they' were penalised nationally for being unclear about which family member(s) they referred to; (3) never simply copy full sentences from the passage ('wholesome lifting') - for example, writing 'I splashed the water at my sister...' instead of 'Tafadzwa splashed water at her sister...' misdirects the subject and loses marks; (4) stick to the 60-word limit - some candidates lost marks for exceeding it. The most common national error in 2022 was writing the summary in the FIRST person ('I splashed water...') instead of the required THIRD person narrative, even though summary writing in English (unlike in some indigenous languages) always requires this third-person convention. Encouragingly, 2022 candidates performed better at summary writing than the 2021 cohort (the year it was introduced to this paper), suggesting more teachers are now teaching the specific demands of English summary writing.
